The test image shows a corn leaf with dark reddish-brown pustules scattered across the leaf surface, with yellow halos visible around some lesions in the upper portion. The pustules appear raised and powdery. This strongly suggests rust disease — either Common Rust or Southern Rust.

Key observations:
- Dark reddish-brown color (not orange/cinnamon)
- Oval to elongate pustules
- Visible on leaf surface with yellow halos
- Relatively scattered, not extremely densely packed

This points toward Common Rust. Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The reference image for Common_Rust shows the same dark reddish-brown pustules scattered across the leaf — matching the test image closely. The color, texture, and distribution are consistent. Southern Rust would show lighter orange/cinnamon pustules more densely packed and almost exclusively on the upper surface.
